dedupe_keys.name: dcpower ics labelled data centre power anomaly dataset

description: DCPower-ICS is a fully synthetic anomaly-detection dataset for data-centre power infrastructure. Vahid Heydari generates utility feed, breakers, automatic transfer, backup generation, batteries, UPS, computing, cooling and sheddable-load variables with a reduced-order simulator. The documented release contains separate 24-hour training and test CSVs sampled at 1 Hz, each with 86,400 rows and 43 columns: time, 40 numeric process variables, a label and a scenario identifier. Twenty-two fault or disturbance scenarios cover maintenance mistakes, commissioning faults, cyber-physical anomalies and operational disturbances. Planned maintenance appears in training data and is labelled normal. The open May 2026 Zenodo release is free under CC BY 4.0; generation and baseline code has a separate MIT archive. There is no real facility location or measured historical period. A limitation is the simplified synthetic physics and deliberately constructed scenario frequencies, which cannot estimate real outage likelihoods. Simulation uses include validating fault detection and maintenance-mode false alarms in data-centre power models. It complements data-atlas-global-data-center-map with controlled operational traces, not facility locations. The earlier rejection solely for being synthetic conflicts with the current reuse rule. No files were downloaded or simulations executed.
